docs.title: GRPC Router
docs.text: GRPC Router is a small component that implements a simple service register to be used for client side service discovery. Services register with the GRPC router, clients request the details of such services in order to discover them and connect directly.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install grpc_router

Requires Python 3.11 or newer.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Start the router (defaults: bind to [::]:50034 with 10 workers):

grpc-router --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 50034 --max-workers 10 --shutdown-grace 5

On SIGTERM or SIGINT (Ctrl+C) the router shuts down gracefully: its health status turns NOT_SERVING, new requests are rejected and in-flight requests get --shutdown-grace seconds to complete. A second signal stops it immediately.

A service registers itself and a client looks it up:

from grpc_router.client.client import GRPCRouterClient
from grpc_router.core.models import HealthCheckType

# in the service
with GRPCRouterClient("router.mydomain.com", 50034) as router:
    router.register_service(
        "myorg.billing.invoices", host="invoices1.mydomain.com", port=8080,
        region="us-east", health_check_type=HealthCheckType.ACTIVE_CLIENT,
    )
    ...  # serve requests; the client pushes heartbeats in the background
    router.deregister_service("myorg.billing.invoices")

# in a client of that service
router = GRPCRouterClient("router.mydomain.com", 50034)
host, port = router.get_service("myorg.billing.invoices", region="us-east")

Instances of the same service are returned round robin, preferring the client's own region.

With HealthCheckType.ACTIVE_CLIENT the client sends heartbeats to the router. A service that misses heartbeats, or reports an error with set_health_status(service_id, HEALTH_STATUS_ERROR, "why"), is taken out of service until it reports a healthy status again (HEALTH_STATUS_GOOD or HEALTH_STATUS_WARNING, from grpc_router.stubs.grpc_router_service_pb2).

If the router forgets a service (it restarted, or the service was out of service and silent for longer than the expiry timeout), the client registers the service again on its next heartbeat.

docs.title: Keeping the register across router restarts
docs.text:
grpc-router --state-file /var/lib/grpc-router/state.json

The router saves its register to that JSON file in the background (at most once per --state-save-interval seconds, default 1, plus on shutdown) and reloads it on start, so clients can find services straight away after a restart, including services without health checks, which never re-register on their own. Restored services have a full health check timeout to send a heartbeat. The file holds the service tokens, so it is created readable by its owner only. Use one file per router. The router also exposes the standard gRPC health checking service, and server reflection (both v1 and v1alpha) so tools like grpcurl can list and describe its API.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Contributions are welcome, and they are greatly appreciated! Every little bit helps, and credit will always be given.

You can contribute in many ways:

docs.title: Report Bugs
docs.text:
Report bugs at https://github.com/ciprianmiclaus2/grpc_router/issues.

If you are reporting a bug, please include:

  • Your operating system name and version.
  • Python version, grpcio and protobuf versions
  • Any other details about your local setup that might be helpful in troubleshooting.
  • Detailed steps to reproduce the bug (a test case is ideal).

docs.title: Fix Bugs
docs.text: Look through the GitHub issues for bugs. Anything tagged with "bug" and "help wanted" is open to whoever wants to implement it.

docs.title: Implement Features
docs.text: Look through the GitHub issues for features. Anything tagged with "enhancement" and "help wanted" is open to whoever wants to implement it.

docs.title: Write Documentation
docs.text: grpc_router could always use more documentation, whether as part of the official grpc_router docs, in docstrings, or even on the web in blog posts, articles, and such.

docs.title: Submit Feedback
docs.text:
The best way to send feedback is to file an issue at https://github.com/ciprianmiclaus2/grpc_router/issues.

If you are proposing a feature:

  • Start with the problem statement (the pain point, what problem are you trying to solve)
  • Explain in detail how it would work.
  • Keep the scope as narrow as possible, to make it easier to implement.
  • Remember that this is a volunteer-driven project, and that contributions are welcome :)

docs.title: Get Started!
docs.text:
Ready to contribute? Here's how to set up grpc_router for local development.

  1. Fork the grpc_router repo on GitHub.
  2. Clone your fork locally
    $ git clone git@github.com:your_name_here/grpc_router.git

  1. Create a venv 

        python -m venv path_to_your_env

  2. Install the package in editable mode with the development dependencies (needs pip >= 25.1 for --group). In the project root folder run: 

        pip install -e . --group dev

  3. Create a branch for local development:

    $ git checkout -b name-of-your-bugfix-or-feature

Now you can make your changes locally.

  1. When you're done making changes, check that your changes pass the linter and the tests:
    $ ruff check .
    $ pytest
  1. Commit your changes and push your branch to GitHub:
    $ git add .
    $ git commit -m "Your detailed description of your changes."
    $ git push origin name-of-your-bugfix-or-feature
  1. Submit a pull request through the GitHub website.

docs.title: Pull Request Guidelines
docs.text:
Before you submit a pull request, check that it meets these guidelines:

  1. The pull request should include tests.
  2. If the pull request adds functionality, the docs should be updated. Put your new functionality into a function with a docstring, and add the feature to the list in README.md.
  3. The pull request should work for Python 3.11 and newer. Check https://github.com/ciprianmiclaus2/grpc_router/actions and make sure that the tests pass for all supported Python versions.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
To run the tests:

    $ pytest -vv tests/

To build and preview the documentation (http://127.0.0.1:8000):

    $ mkdocs serve

The docs are published to GitHub Pages by the Documentation workflow when a release is published.

If you change proto/grpc_router_service.proto, regenerate the stubs with:

    $ ./gen_stubs.sh

Regenerating embeds the protobuf/grpcio versions of your grpcio-tools in the generated code, so bump the lower bounds in pyproject.toml to match (see the comments in gen_stubs.sh).

docs.title: Deploying
docs.text:
A reminder for the maintainers on how to deploy. Make sure all your changes are committed (including an entry in HISTORY.md and the version bump in pyproject.toml). Then tag and push:

$ git tag v<version>
$ git push
$ git push --tags

Then publish a GitHub release for the tag; GitHub Actions builds the package and uploads it to PyPI (trusted publishing), and publishes the docs for the release's minor version to GitHub Pages (the gh-pages branch).

docs.title: gRPC API
docs.text:
The router's API is defined in proto/grpc_router_service.proto. Python services and clients can use GRPCRouterClient; from other languages, generate a client from the proto file, or explore the API of a running router with server reflection, e.g. with grpcurl.

A service written in another language has to do what GRPCRouterClient does for ACTIVE_CLIENT instances: call PushHealthStatus regularly (well within the router's health check timeout, 5 minutes by default), and call RegisterService again when PushHealthStatus returns NOT_FOUND. See Health checks.

syntax = "proto3";

package grpcrouter;


option java_package = "com.grpcrouter.service";
option java_multiple_files = true;


service GRPCRouterService {

    // Register a service endpoint
    //
    // Called by a service that wants to advertise its services to clients.
    // Provides a service_id which ideally should be a dot separated namespace representing
    // the service but it can be anything, e.g.: org.suborg.scope1.service1
    // It also has information about how clients can connect directly to the service (ie host/port)
    // The service gets back a service_token which it can use to communicate with the grpc router.
    // A registration replaces the entries of the same service_id, host and port that look dead
    // (e.g. the same service restarted): entries that are out of service, that missed heartbeats or
    // that have no health checks.
    rpc RegisterService(ServiceRegistrationRequest) returns (ServiceRegistrationResponse) {}

    // Deregister a service endpoint
    //
    // Called by a service when it exits and it no longer serves client requests.
    // The service should pass its service_token which was obtained at registration.
    rpc DeregisterService(ServiceDeregistrationRequest) returns (ServiceDeregistrationResponse) {}

    // Get the detail of a service
    //
    // Returns the details of a registered service when called by a client.
    // The client then can connect directly to that service.
    // The client specifies the service_id which is service register for.
    // When multiple services are registered for the same service_id, they are returned in a simple
    // round-robin fashion.
    rpc GetRegisteredService(GetRegisteredServiceRequest) returns (GetRegisteredServiceResponse) {}


    // Client pushes the health status periodically
    //
    // This is used in the ACTIVE_CLIENT modus operandi for clients to
    // push health info to the grpc router.
    // Clients using this method must specify health check type ACTIVE_CLIENT
    // when registering.
    //
    // A service that misses heartbeats for longer than the router's health check timeout,
    // or that reports HEALTH_STATUS_ERROR, is taken out of service: it is no longer returned
    // by GetRegisteredService. It keeps its service_token and should keep pushing (ERROR
    // included) while it is out of service; it goes back in service as soon as it pushes any
    // status other than HEALTH_STATUS_ERROR. A service that is out of service and pushes
    // nothing for longer than the router's expiry timeout is forgotten, and gets NOT_FOUND
    // until it registers again.
    rpc PushHealthStatus(HealthInfoRequest) returns (HealthInfoResponse) {}

}


enum HealthCheckType {
    HEALTH_CHECK_NONE = 0;  // no health checks
    HEALTH_CHECK_ACTIVE_CLIENT = 1;  // client will push health notifications to the server
    HEALTH_CHECK_PASSIVE_CLIENT = 2;  // client implements the health grpc interface and server should poll/watch
}


enum HealthStatus {
    HEALTH_STATUS_UNKNOWN = 0;
    HEALTH_STATUS_GOOD = 1;
    HEALTH_STATUS_WARNING = 2;
    HEALTH_STATUS_ERROR = 3;
}


message ServiceEndpoint {
    string host = 1;  // hostname of the service
    int32 port = 2;  // port of the service
}


message ServiceMetadata {
    string region = 1;
    int32 slots = 2;
    HealthCheckType health_check_type = 3;
}

message ServiceRegistrationRequest {
    string service_id = 1;  // identifier of the service that the clients will use
    ServiceEndpoint endpoint = 2;
    ServiceMetadata metadata = 3;
}


message ServiceRegistrationResponse {
    string service_token = 1;
}


message ServiceDeregistrationRequest {
    string service_id = 1;
    string service_token = 2;
}


message ServiceDeregistrationResponse {
}

message ServiceHints {
    string region = 1;
}

message GetRegisteredServiceRequest {
    string service_id = 1;
    ServiceHints hints = 2;
}


message GetRegisteredServiceResponse {
    string service_id = 1;
    ServiceEndpoint endpoint = 2;
}


message HealthInfoRequest {
    string service_id = 1;
    string service_token = 2;
    HealthStatus status = 3;
    string description = 4;
}

message HealthInfoResponse{
}

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
A service picks how the router checks that it is alive when it registers, with a HealthCheckType:

  • NONE: no checks. The instance stays registered until it deregisters, or until an instance registers again at the same address.
  • ACTIVE_CLIENT: the service sends heartbeats to the router. GRPCRouterClient sends them in a background thread every HEALTH_PUSH_FREQUENCY_SECONDS (3 minutes), and straight away when set_health_status() is called.
  • PASSIVE_CLIENT: the router would poll the service. Not implemented yet: such instances are accepted but never checked, so they are taken out of service after the health check timeout.

docs.title: Lifecycle of an ACTIVE_CLIENT instance
docs.text:
An instance is either in service (the router hands it out to clients) or out of service (it is still known to the router, with its token, but not handed out).

Event Result Registration In service. Heartbeat with GOOD, WARNING or UNKNOWN Stays in service, or goes back in service if it was out. Heartbeat with ERROR Taken out of service, or stays out. No heartbeat for health_check_timeout (default 5 minutes) Taken out of service. Out of service and no heartbeat at all, ERROR included, for unhealthy_expiry_timeout (default 15 minutes) Forgotten: the next heartbeat gets NOT_FOUND. Deregistration Removed, whether in or out of service.

The router checks the timeouts every 30 seconds, so they can be exceeded by up to that much.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text:
from grpc_router.core.models import HealthStatus

router.set_health_status("myorg.billing.invoices", HealthStatus.ERROR, "Database down.")
# ... later, once the problem is fixed
router.set_health_status("myorg.billing.invoices", HealthStatus.GOOD, "")

Keep the client running while the service is out of service: its ERROR heartbeats tell the router the instance is still alive, so it is not forgotten. The router never probes the service itself, so the service has to report when it is healthy again.

docs.title: When the router forgets an instance
docs.text: If the router restarted without a state file, or forgot an instance that was out of service and silent for too long, the instance's next heartbeat gets NOT_FOUND. GRPCRouterClient then registers the service again, with a new token, and sends its current status at once: an instance in ERROR goes straight back out of service.

docs.title: When a service restarts
docs.text: A restarted service registers again and gets a new token. The registration replaces the entries of the same service_id, host and port that look dead: entries that are out of service, that missed their heartbeats, or that have no health checks. An entry that still looks healthy is kept, as it could be another live process behind the same address; if it is a leftover, it misses its heartbeats and drops out within the health check timeout.

The 0.3.0 package on PyPI was broken (see below): upgrade to 0.4.0. The gRPC API (proto/grpc_router_service.proto) is unchanged, so 0.3.0 clients work with a 0.4.0 router and the reverse, but upgrade the clients too: 0.3.0 clients stop sending heartbeats after 3 minutes (see Fixes).

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+ is now required (3.9 and 3.10 are end of life).
  • Minimum dependency versions are now declared: grpcio>=1.66.2, grpcio-reflection>=1.66.2, grpcio-health-checking>=1.66.2, protobuf>=5.27.2 (tested up to protobuf 7).
  • Reporting HEALTH_STATUS_ERROR now takes an ACTIVE_CLIENT service out of service; it used to be stored while the service was still handed out to clients. As after missed heartbeats, the service keeps its token and goes back in service as soon as it pushes any other status (GOOD, WARNING, UNKNOWN).
  • Out of service instances are now forgotten after ConfigOptions.unhealthy_expiry_timeout seconds (default 900) without any health push; they used to be kept forever.
  • A registration now replaces the entries for the same service_id, host and port that look dead: out of service, missed heartbeats, or no health checks. A restarted service no longer leaves stale or duplicate entries.
  • The client now registers a service again, with a new token, when its heartbeat gets NOT_FOUND. A token kept from register_service() can therefore become outdated; the client itself always uses the current one.
  • The router no longer enables SO_REUSEPORT: starting a second router on a port already in use now fails instead of silently splitting the service register between the two processes.
  • GRPCRouterClient.HEALTh_PUSh_FREQUENCY_SECONDS is renamed to HEALTH_PUSH_FREQUENCY_SECONDS; the old name is kept as a deprecated alias.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The published package: the 0.3.0 wheel only contained grpc_router/server.py and was missing the client, core and stubs subpackages, so it could not be imported. CI now tests the installed wheel and the sdist.
  • ACTIVE_CLIENT heartbeats: the client's heartbeat thread exited the first time HEALTH_PUSH_FREQUENCY_SECONDS (3 minutes) passed without a set_health_status() call, so services that did not keep calling it were evicted after health_check_timeout (5 minutes) and never came back. The client now sends heartbeats until close().
  • ERROR heartbeats from an out of service instance are now accepted; they used to fail with NOT_FOUND.
  • Deregistering an out of service instance now removes it.
  • Re-registration by health push now checks that the token belongs to the pushed service_id.
  • The PushHealthStatus error message for an empty token ("service_token", was "service_context").
  • A race where concurrent registrations could start more than one health check thread.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Optional write-behind persistence of the register (--state-file, --state-save-interval; ConfigOptions.state_file, state_save_interval): a human readable JSON file with the time of the last save, written atomically and readable by its owner only, reloaded on start. Restored instances get a fresh health check timeout. A file that cannot be loaded is moved aside to <name>.bad-<timestamp> and the router starts empty.
  • Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT: the health status turns NOT_SERVING, new RPCs are rejected and in-flight RPCs get a grace period (--shutdown-grace, ConfigOptions.shutdown_grace, default 5s) to complete; a second signal stops immediately. The router now logs startup, shutdown and state restores.
  • Server reflection is served as both grpc.reflection.v1 and grpc.reflection.v1alpha, so clients that only speak v1 (recent grpcurl, Postman, etc.) work.
  • Documentation site: https://ciprianmiclaus2.github.io/grpc_router/ (running the router, health checks, gRPC and Python API).
  • grpc-router command line entry point to start the router.
  • grpc_router.server.create_server(config) builds a router without blocking (serve still blocks).
  • GRPCRouterClient caches its stub, and gains close() and context manager support.
  • Type information: py.typed and generated .pyi stubs for the protobuf messages.

docs.title: Packaging and tooling
docs.text:
• [build-system] table, SPDX license metadata, PEP 735 dependency groups (pip install -e . --group dev), sdist with the tests, proto and stub generation script.
  • ruff replaces flake8; GitHub Actions updated, with a test matrix for Python 3.11 to 3.15, a minimum versions job, a packaging job and a docs build; the docs are published to GitHub Pages on each release.

• Support for active client health check type (passive not yet implemented)
    • This is when the client pushes heathbeats into the server
    • If the server detects a missed client heartbeat, it automatically marks the client as unhealthy and does not return it
    • If the same client recovers, the server marks it back healthy
  • Fix the service registration implementation to be thread safe

• Enable health checking service on the grpc router
  • Enable reflection in the server
  • Fix the server cli -h conflicting with --help and the port not being parsed as an int

Initial release of the grpc_router, a service discovery tool for grpc services. Allows grpc services to register/deregister and clients to lookup services based on a service_id which should ideally consist of a dot separated namespace, e.g. domain.scope.service. In practice, the service_id can be any string, there is no inherent limitation. Services operate with a concept of region, which can allow clients to connect preferentially to the services in their own region, with a fallback to another region if there's no services running in their own region.

docs.title: From the command line
docs.text:
grpc-router --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 50034
Option Default -n, --hostname [::] Hostname or address to bind to ([::]: all interfaces). -p, --port 50034 Port to bind to. -w, --max-workers 10 Maximum number of requests handled concurrently. -g, --shutdown-grace 5 Seconds in-flight requests get to complete on SIGTERM/SIGINT. -s, --state-file JSON file to persist the register to (see below). Disabled by default. --state-save-interval 1 The state file is saved at most once per this many seconds.

python -m grpc_router.server takes the same options.

The router logs to stderr, including the start, the shutdown and the restore of a state file.

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
Some settings are only available from Python, through ConfigOptions: the region fallbacks, health_check_timeout and unhealthy_expiry_timeout.

from grpc_router.core.models import ConfigOptions
from grpc_router.server import serve

serve(ConfigOptions(
    hostname="[::]", port=50034, max_workers=10,
    allow_cross_region_connectivity=False,  # never route a client to another region
    health_check_timeout=60,
    state_file="/var/lib/grpc-router/state.json",
))

serve() blocks until the router stops. create_server() returns a router that is not started yet, e.g. to run it inside another program or in tests.

docs.title: Regions
docs.text:
Each instance registers with a region; the empty string is the global region. A client asking for a service in a region gets, in order of preference:

  1. an instance of its own region;
  2. an instance of the global region, unless allow_global_region is off;
  3. an instance of any other region, unless allow_cross_region_connectivity is off.

With allow_global_region off, registering without a region is rejected. Instances are returned round robin within each of these groups.

docs.title: Shutting down
docs.text:
On SIGTERM or SIGINT (Ctrl+C) the router shuts down gracefully:

  1. its gRPC health status turns NOT_SERVING, so health checking load balancers and watchers stop sending it traffic;
  2. it rejects new requests and gives in-flight requests --shutdown-grace seconds to complete;
  3. it saves the state file, if any, and exits with status 0.

A second signal stops it immediately.

docs.title: Keeping the register across restarts
docs.text:
The register lives in memory. With --state-file, the router also saves it to a JSON file and reloads it on start:

grpc-router --state-file /var/lib/grpc-router/state.json
  • Write behind: registrations, deregistrations, services going in or out of service and status changes are saved in the background, at most once per --state-save-interval, and once more on shutdown. Plain heartbeats do not rewrite the file.
  • On start, every restored instance gets a full health check timeout to send its next heartbeat, however old the file is: instances that died while the router was down then drop out through the normal health checks. Out of service instances stay out of service.
  • Recovery without the file: a crash can lose the changes of the last save interval, and a router started without a state file knows nothing. Services with health checks recover on their own: when a heartbeat gets NOT_FOUND, GRPCRouterClient registers the service again. Services without health checks only come back with the state file, or when they register again.
  • The file is written atomically (a temporary file renamed over it) and is only readable by its owner, as it holds the service tokens.
  • A file that cannot be loaded is moved aside to <name>.bad-<timestamp> and the router starts empty. If the file cannot be written, the router does not start.
  • Use one file per router: two routers sharing a file overwrite each other's state.

The file is meant to be readable:

{
  "version": 1,
  "saved_at": "2026-11-27T13:17:34.555810+00:00",
  "instances": [
    {
      "service_id": "myorg.billing.invoices",
      "host": "invoices2.mydomain.com",
      "port": 8080,
      "region": "us-east",
      "slots": 10,
      "health_check_type": "ACTIVE_CLIENT",
      "service_token": "4b93c187-edc2-4116-afca-95ede07b603e",
      "in_service": false,
      "health_status": "ERROR",
      "description": "Database down."
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Health and reflection
docs.text:
Besides its own API, the router serves:

  • the standard gRPC health checking service (grpc.health.v1.Health), for the service grpcrouter.GRPCRouterService and for the server as a whole ("");
  • server reflection, in both the v1 and v1alpha versions, so tools like grpcurl can list and describe its API:
grpcurl -plaintext localhost:50034 list
grpcurl -plaintext localhost:50034 describe grpcrouter.GRPCRouterService

Only one router can listen on a port: a second router started on a port already in use fails to start, instead of silently splitting the register between the two processes.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
• Client: GRPCRouterClient, used by services to register and by their clients to look them up.
  • Server and configuration: serve, create_server, ConfigOptions, and the HealthCheckType and HealthStatus enums.

The generated protobuf and gRPC code is in grpc_router.stubs (see the gRPC API).

docs.title: GRPCRouterClient
docs.text:
Client of the grpc router, for services (to register) and for their clients (to look them up).

Registered ACTIVE_CLIENT services get heartbeats sent in a background thread every HEALTH_PUSH_FREQUENCY_SECONDS, and straight away when set_health_status is called. If the router no longer knows a service (it restarted without a state file, or the service was out of service and silent for too long), the client registers it again on its next heartbeat.

Use it as a context manager, or call close when done, to stop the heartbeats and close the channel.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default host str

Host of the router.

required port int

Port of the router.

required grpc_service_config dict[str, Any] | None

gRPC service config for the channel, e.g. its retry policy. Defaults to DEFAULT_GRPC_SERVICE_CONFIG, which retries failed calls up to 5 times with backoff.

None

docs.title: channel property
docs.text:
channel: Channel

The gRPC channel to the router, created on first use.

docs.title: stub property
docs.text:
stub: GRPCRouterServiceStub

The generated gRPC stub of the router service, for direct calls.

docs.title: register_service
docs.text:
register_service(service_id: str, host: str, port: int, region: str = '', slots: int = 10, health_check_type: int = 0) -> str

Register a service instance with the router.

Registering the same service_id again with the same client is a no-op that returns the existing token.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default service_id str

Name of the service, ideally a dot separated namespace, e.g. "myorg.billing.invoices".

required host str

Host clients connect to.

required port int

Port clients connect to.

required region str

Region of the instance; "" is the global region.

'' slots int

Capacity hint of the instance (not used by the router yet).

10 health_check_type int

A HealthCheckType; ACTIVE_CLIENT starts sending heartbeats.

0

Returns:

Type Description str

The service token. It can change if the client has to register the service again.

docs.title: deregister_service
docs.text:
deregister_service(service_id: str) -> None

Deregister a service registered by this client (no-op if it is not registered).

docs.title: get_service
docs.text:
get_service(service_id: str, region: str = '') -> tuple[str, int]

Look up an instance of a service, round robin.

The router prefers instances of the given region, then of the global region, then of any region, depending on its configuration.

Returns:

Type Description tuple[str, int]

The (host, port) to connect to.

Raises:

Type Description RpcError

With code NOT_FOUND if no instance is in service.

docs.title: set_health_status
docs.text:
set_health_status(service_id: str, status: int, description: str) -> None

Set the health status of a service registered by this client, and push it straight away.

HealthStatus.ERROR takes the service out of service until a healthy status is set again.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default service_id str

The registered service.

required status int

A HealthStatus (or the equivalent HEALTH_STATUS_* value of the generated stubs).

required description str

Free text, e.g. why the service is unhealthy.

required

docs.title: close
docs.text:
close() -> None

Stop pushing health statuses and close the channel. Services are not deregistered.

docs.title: serve
docs.text:
serve(config: ConfigOptions) -> None

Run the grpc router until it is stopped.

When called from the main thread, SIGTERM and SIGINT trigger a graceful shutdown: the health status turns NOT_SERVING, new RPCs are rejected and in-flight RPCs get config.shutdown_grace seconds to complete. A second signal stops immediately.

docs.title: create_server
docs.text:
create_server(config: ConfigOptions) -> grpc.Server

Create a (not yet started) grpc router server bound to config.hostname:config.port.

With config.state_file the register is loaded from it now and saved in the background; use serve() to also get the final save on shutdown.

docs.title: ConfigOptions dataclass
docs.text:
Configuration of the router.

Attributes:

Name Type Description hostname str

Hostname or address to bind to, e.g. "[::]" for all interfaces.

port int

Port to bind to.

max_workers int

Maximum number of requests handled concurrently.

allow_global_region bool

Allow services to register without a region (the global region), and fall back to global services when a client's region has none.

allow_cross_region_connectivity bool

Fall back to services of other regions when neither the client's region nor the global region has any.

health_check_timeout int

Seconds without a heartbeat after which an ACTIVE_CLIENT service is taken out of service.

unhealthy_expiry_timeout int

Seconds without any health push after which an out of service instance is forgotten; it then has to register again.

shutdown_grace float

Seconds in-flight requests get to complete on SIGTERM/SIGINT.

state_file str | None

Path of the JSON file to save the register to and reload it from on start; None disables persistence.

state_save_interval float

The state file is saved at most once per this many seconds.

docs.title: HealthCheckType
docs.text:
How the router checks that a registered service is alive.

Attributes:

Name Type Description NONE

No health checks: the service stays registered until it deregisters.

ACTIVE_CLIENT

The service pushes heartbeats to the router (GRPCRouterClient does it).

PASSIVE_CLIENT

The router polls the service. Not implemented yet.

docs.title: HealthStatus
docs.text:
Health status a service reports with its heartbeats.

ERROR takes the service out of service; any other status keeps it in, or puts it back in, service.
